title: Singleton
summary: Recognize a single shared instance; prefer passing it in over hiding it.

parts.rule: Singleton means exactly one shared instance of a type in a process. Prefer constructing that instance once at the composition root and passing it to dependents. body:
Rule. Singleton means exactly one shared instance of a type in a process. Prefer constructing that instance once at the composition root and passing it to dependents. Hidden global accessors make testing and lifetimes harder. If you truly need a process-wide resource, say why and how tests replace it.

Why it matters. Classic singleton static getInstance hides dependencies and freezes order of initialization. Interviewers increasingly want explicit injection of the shared logger, clock, or connection pool instead of ambient globals.

Worked example. Bad: Database.getInstance().query inside twelve classes — tests cannot swap a fake without reflection. Better: main creates one DbPool from config and passes it into UserRepo and OrderRepo constructors. Those classes store the pool reference; they never fetch a global. Metrics registry can be similar: one Registry built at startup, injected where counters are recorded. Thread-safe lazy static singletons are still globals with a costume. For a true hardware printer spooler that the OS exposes once, wrapping it behind an injected Port keeps your code honest.  Walk one concrete path with numbers before generalizing. Keep the tone focused and honest.  Walk one concrete path with numbers before generalizing. Keep the tone focused and honest.  Walk one concrete path with numbers before generalizing. Keep the tone focused and honest.  Walk one concrete path with numbers before generalizing. Keep the tone focused and honest.

When to use. Use a single shared instance for process-wide connection pools, metric registries, and config snapshots. Construct it in main or a DI container and pass it down.

When to refuse. Refuse static getInstance as the default for domain services. Refuse singletons that carry mutable request state. Refuse singletons that make unit tests need global reset rituals. Refuse claiming singleton when what you need is just a long-lived instance owned by a clear parent.
